caption: What if all 1.46 billion Indians jumped at exactly the same second? India is the world's most populous country, with about 1.46 billion people (UN, 2025). Together we weigh roughly 70 million tonnes. A 30 cm jump keeps you in the air for about half a second. Sounds huge, but Earth's mass is about 5.97 trillion trillion kg, roughly 80 trillion times more than all of us combined. So our push would shift the planet by only a few femtometres, about the width of an atom's nucleus, and when we land it moves straight back. Net change: zero. Fun fact: on 7 September 2001, about a million UK school kids really tried a 'Giant Jump' for science while seismometers listened. Earth stayed calm. The uncle downstairs? Different story.
